one-line thesis: A deliberately messy optical quarter: PNB Housing switched disbursement recognition from **cheque handover to cheque realization**, which cut reported Q1 disbursement growth to **+18% YoY at ₹5,882 crores** versus **"a strong 56% Y-o-Y growth"** on the comparable old basis — so the reported book growth of 15% understates the run-rate and management says *"We will catch up on our growth rate from next quarter onwards."* The real operating debate is mix: Affordable disbursed only **₹555 crores** (*"currently less than the target level"*) while Prime and Emerging carried the quarter, yet management is unmoved on **18–20% book growth and 50–60% Affordable growth** for FY27 on the back of a new CBO and a July that is *"much, much promising than my month of June"*. Margin is the second leg: NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to **3.50%** but spread held at **2.12%**, and management repeatedly asserts *"margin have bottomed out and yield is also bottomed out"* with improvement only from **H2 FY27**.

> **One-offs / distortions to call out explicitly:**
> 1. **Disbursement recognition change** — *"starting this quarter, disbursements are being recognized based on check realization rather than check handover basis."* This is the single biggest distortion in the print: 56% → 18% YoY disbursement growth, and ~18% → 15% loan-book growth. Not a lost sale — *"whatever hit we have taken in Q1 will give us fruit in Q2."*
> 2. **7 bps Q4 FY26 NIM true-up** — *"Q4 being a shorter quarter, only 90 days… it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4"*; adjusted for it, *"the gap is only 12 bps in the current quarter."*
> 3. **Legacy fraud classification** — *"During the quarter, legacy account was classified as fraud. The exposure had already been fully provided in the FY 22-23 and therefore, it has no incremental financial impact on the company."* (Analyst Gaurav Khandelwal referenced *"the fraud account of INR 420 crores"*; management did not restate the amount.)
> 4. **OTS write-off** — *"There are some regular OTS settlements, etc which we do. So that has given some hit of around INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores"*, on the legacy Prime/Emerging pool; sits in write-offs, not ECL.
> 5. **Negative credit cost is a recovery artefact**, not underwriting — driven by the ₹67 crores written-off-pool recovery against a shrinking ~₹340 crores residual pool.

risks & watch-items:
1. **The Q2 catch-up must actually land.** The whole quarter's optics are deferred, not lost — but only if realization follows: overall net disbursement *"near 60%-70% higher"* than Q1 and Affordable *"2.5 to 2.6x"*. Miss this and FY27's 18–20% book guidance is at risk.
2. **Incremental cost of borrowing +18 bps and still elevated.** Management concedes it *"still remains elevated"*; the NIM-bottoming call depends on mix-driven yield gains offsetting it.
3. **Pending rating upgrades are unpriced and undated.** *"CARE is already done. ICRA is underway. I think we are expecting very soon. ICRA and CRISIL is underway."* Worth *"around 10 basis points at least"* on CoF — but no date was given (deliberately excluded from `near_term_trigger`, see §10 rule).
4. **Affordable is behind plan, and the fix is a brand-new leadership team.** ₹555 crores is *"currently less than the target level"*; the recovery case is entirely *"under new leadership team, particularly new CBO"* with one month (July) of evidence.
5. **Prime is being pushed up-risk.** More self-employed, more non-home-loan. Management's answer is bench quality and improving sequential delinquency, but this is the structural risk to watch over FY28–29 rather than FY27.
6. **30+/90+ ticked up.** *"Minor increase seen in 30+ and 90+ is cyclical in nature and are expected to come down in Q2"* — a dated, checkable claim.
7. **Negative credit cost has a finite life.** The written-off pool is down to ~₹340 crores retail; management guides negative for FY27 only, then normalization — ROA guidance already steps down to 2.3–2.35%.
8. **Fraud-account recovery is entirely optional upside** — nothing budgeted for FY27, timing unknown: *"I can't comment at this point of time because it will depend on the — when I get the buyer."*
9. **Macro:** RBI held repo at 5.25% but cut FY27 GDP *"from 6.9% to 6.66% in its June 2026 policy review"*; the quarter was *"characterized by heightened global uncertainty arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to higher crude oil prices, increased market volatility and tighter liquidity conditions."*
management quality / tone: Confident and unusually specific for a quarter that optically missed. The MD volunteered the recognition change up front rather than letting analysts find it, gave a quantified Q2 bridge (2.5–2.6x Affordable, 60–70% overall net) instead of hiding behind guidance, and refused to soften the Affordable guidance when pressed (*"my guidance will not change, it will continue"*). The CFO handled the NIM walk in full detail (12 bps + 7 bps, plus the Q4 day-count true-up mechanics) without deflecting. Two tells of candour: the admission that Affordable is *"currently less than the target level"*, and the flat refusal to quantify fraud recoveries. The main watch on tone is **repeated reliance on a single unaudited month** — July is cited five separate times as the proof of the turnaround, which is a thin evidentiary base for a 50–60% full-year Affordable growth commitment. Also note the MD twice nudged above his own guidance (*"we should do much better than what we have given guidance"*), which raises the bar he will be judged against.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The 56% vs 18% gap is the whole quarter.** Two headline numbers for the same business, differing only by ~2 months of cheque clearing. Anyone comparing PNBHOUSING's Q1 disbursement growth to peers on a like-for-like basis must use 56%, and the Q2 print will be flattered by the same mechanic in reverse — the sequential number will be structurally overstated.
- **Prime's yield improvement is up-risking, dressed as mix optimization.** *"we have migrated from the composition of more salary to the… rationalized, self-employed segment"* and *"increased our composition from home loan to non-home loan."* ~10–15 bps of the yield came from consuming regulatory (PVC) headroom, not from franchise strength. Absent it, Prime yields would have been *"stable"* at best.
- **The NIM decline is self-inflicted and arguably good.** 12 of the 19 bps came from *deliberately* levering up an over-capitalized balance sheet (3.6 → 3.75 average) — an ROE-accretive trade the P&L presents as margin compression. Only 7 bps was accounting noise, and none of it was competitive pressure.
- **Negative credit cost is flattering a −4pp NII/PAT gap.** NII +6%, PPOP +9%, PAT only +4% — the recovery tailwind (−12 bps) is running *alongside*, not covering, the ₹10–12 crore OTS write-off and the ECL build. Strip both and the underlying earnings quality is thinner than "negative credit cost" suggests.
- **Affordable's quality improved even as its volume disappointed.** BT-in collapsed 10.5% → 3.4%, i.e. the shortfall is in *new-to-market* originations, not in a loss of refinanced book — the harder but more durable kind of growth.
- **The "no new branches" stance is the real opex story.** Three new businesses (Affordable-via-Prime, micro-housing, Emerging Developer Finance) are all being launched into the existing 404-branch footprint, which is why opex/ATA fell below 1% while headcount investment rose.
- **A fraud classification with zero P&L impact is a *recovery* event, not a credit event** — fully provided in FY22-23, and management argues classification *accelerates* resolution: *"generally it expedites because there are legal recourse. Because till the time you take this step, the customer will never come forward to discuss and close it."*

one-line thesis: A deliberately messy optical quarter: PNB Housing switched disbursement recognition from **cheque handover to cheque realization**, which cut reported Q1 disbursement growth to **+18% YoY at ₹5,882 crores** versus **"a strong 56% Y-o-Y growth"** on the comparable old basis — so the reported book growth of 15% understates the run-rate and management says *"We will catch up on our growth rate from next quarter onwards."* The real operating debate is mix: Affordable disbursed only **₹555 crores** (*"currently less than the target level"*) while Prime and Emerging carried the quarter, yet management is unmoved on **18–20% book growth and 50–60% Affordable growth** for FY27 on the back of a new CBO and a July that is *"much, much promising than my month of June"*. Margin is the second leg: NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to **3.50%** but spread held at **2.12%**, and management repeatedly asserts *"margin have bottomed out and yield is also bottomed out"* with improvement only from **H2 FY27**.

> **One-offs / distortions to call out explicitly:**
> 1. **Disbursement recognition change** — *"starting this quarter, disbursements are being recognized based on check realization rather than check handover basis."* This is the single biggest distortion in the print: 56% → 18% YoY disbursement growth, and ~18% → 15% loan-book growth. Not a lost sale — *"whatever hit we have taken in Q1 will give us fruit in Q2."*
> 2. **7 bps Q4 FY26 NIM true-up** — *"Q4 being a shorter quarter, only 90 days… it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4"*; adjusted for it, *"the gap is only 12 bps in the current quarter."*
> 3. **Legacy fraud classification** — *"During the quarter, legacy account was classified as fraud. The exposure had already been fully provided in the FY 22-23 and therefore, it has no incremental financial impact on the company."* (Analyst Gaurav Khandelwal referenced *"the fraud account of INR 420 crores"*; management did not restate the amount.)
> 4. **OTS write-off** — *"There are some regular OTS settlements, etc which we do. So that has given some hit of around INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores"*, on the legacy Prime/Emerging pool; sits in write-offs, not ECL.
> 5. **Negative credit cost is a recovery artefact**, not underwriting — driven by the ₹67 crores written-off-pool recovery against a shrinking ~₹340 crores residual pool.

6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Capital as an optionality buffer** — CAR 28.26% / Tier 1 27.87% against period-end leverage of 3.72x. Management is deliberately *spending* this cushion (average leverage 3.6 → 3.75) to fund growth, i.e. NIM dilution here is a chosen use of surplus capital, not distress.
- **Underwriting bench in self-employed mortgages** — the defence offered for pushing Prime up-risk into self-employed and non-home-loan: *"while my yield has gone up, I would say sequentially even my delinquency in Prime and Emerging has improved from last quarter because team is a very seasoned underwriting team… we have good seasoned expertise team in underwriting, especially in the self-employed segment."* Evidenced by the direction of 30+/90+ within Prime/Emerging, though the aggregate 30+/90+ did tick up.
- **Regulatory headroom as a pricing lever** — the Prime mix shift into non-home-loan was executed *"because we were having a good cushion in terms of PVC norms. So regulatory also we were very much in line."* — i.e. unused regulatory capacity converted directly into ~10–15 bps of yield.
- **Distribution + own-tech rails** — 404 branches with the ability to originate a *different* segment (Affordable) off existing Prime/Emerging infrastructure at no incremental opex; 100% of fresh disbursals on the in-house LOS.

- **NIM 3.50%, −19 bps QoQ**, fully attributed: *"12 bps is attributable to increase in leverage and 7 bps in true-up impact of Q4 FY26."* CFO's fuller version adds the asset-side drag: *"there is also a flow-through impact. If you see, Q4 generally is very high on disbursements, and most of that got realized in the current quarter, and hence it actually translated into higher borrowings during the current quarter. Plus, there is an impact of also on the overall yield being slightly lower while the loan book yield has improved, but overall yield has slightly moderated due to lower investment yields."*
- **Spread held at 2.12%**, book and incremental — *"Despite the prevailing headwinds, we maintained our spread at 2.12%, demonstrating resilience in our business model and disciplined pricing approach."*
- **Yield inflected, barely:** 9.47% → **9.48%**. The bull case rests on mix, not rates: *"there is no further drop expected on the yield perspective, it is only expected to go up. And hence the only positive impact that we see from now on is on account of mix change."*
- **Funding cost is the live headwind:** book CoB 7.35% → **7.36%**, but incremental CoB **+18 bps**. Asked whether it has cooled: *"there is some improvement versus what it was, let's say, at the beginning of the previous quarter, but still it remains elevated."* Offsets claimed: *"now Q2 onwards, with higher contribution of Affordable, CF business and Emerging business, we feel that we will be able to offset the impacts, if any, of cost of borrowing, as well as of any further impact of leverage."*
- **Why last year's mix shift did NOT show in yield** (Renish's challenge — book yield down ~50 bps YoY despite a richer mix): *"last one year, if you see, there is a change in the repo rate also, and the interest rate environment also was different… So our incremental yields have gone down in line with the industry trend. So hence you did not see that kind of a transition impact on the overall book yield."*
- **Opex leverage is real:** opex +10% YoY to ₹237 crores but opex/ATA below 1% (from 1.08% in Q4 FY26); PPOP +9% on NII +6%.
- **Recognition change is yield-neutral, income-negative:** *"The impact is only on interest income for the quarter"*; and *"if you are not booking the underlying loan, you are not booking that income also. So it will not impact your yield. It will impact the absolute income, but it will not impact the yield."*
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Branches: 404, +12 in Q1.** The stated expansion model is now *anti*-capex — new segments (Affordable via Prime/Emerging, micro-housing via Affordable) are to be run off existing branches: *"I don't think at this point of time we need to open more number of branches. We will leverage our existing branches to contain our opex also."*
- **People, not property, is the FY27 investment:** *"the major investment which this year we have done in Affordable business only. So even N minus 2… under the CBO we have strengthened our team all across geographies. So we have 2 national-level resources also who are managing businesses who have vintage of almost more than 20-25 years in mortgage industry."*
- **Technology build-out** continues (SFDC LOS, Infinity onboarding app, Legality e-sign, Voice AI, in-house computing intelligence platform) — no rupee capex figure given on the call.
- **Slippage watch:** the Affordable ramp is now a *people/productivity* project with a July-dated proof point, so the slippage risk shows up in monthly disbursement, not in a commissioning date.
capital allocation:
- **Capital position:** CAR 28.26%, Tier 1 27.87%, net worth ₹19,800 crores, book value ~₹760 — *"Our capital position remains strong."* No capital raise, buyback or dividend was discussed on this call.
- **Deployment path** is leverage-up into higher-yield retail: average leverage 3.6 → 3.75, mix to 45% Affordable+Emerging by FY27 and ~50% by FY28, CF capped at 3%.
- **Return framework:** ROE 11.44% on ROA 2.37% — the gap is exactly the under-levered balance sheet; management is guiding ROA down (2.4% → 2.3–2.35%) as credit cost normalizes, implying the ROE story has to come from leverage and mix rather than from asset returns.
- **New capital uses this quarter:** Emerging Developer Finance (₹71 crores) and loan buyouts (₹146 crores) — both explicitly yield-accretive.
risks & watch-items:
1. **The Q2 catch-up must actually land.** The whole quarter's optics are deferred, not lost — but only if realization follows: overall net disbursement *"near 60%-70% higher"* than Q1 and Affordable *"2.5 to 2.6x"*. Miss this and FY27's 18–20% book guidance is at risk.
2. **Incremental cost of borrowing +18 bps and still elevated.** Management concedes it *"still remains elevated"*; the NIM-bottoming call depends on mix-driven yield gains offsetting it.
3. **Pending rating upgrades are unpriced and undated.** *"CARE is already done. ICRA is underway. I think we are expecting very soon. ICRA and CRISIL is underway."* Worth *"around 10 basis points at least"* on CoF — but no date was given (deliberately excluded from `near_term_trigger`, see §10 rule).
4. **Affordable is behind plan, and the fix is a brand-new leadership team.** ₹555 crores is *"currently less than the target level"*; the recovery case is entirely *"under new leadership team, particularly new CBO"* with one month (July) of evidence.
5. **Prime is being pushed up-risk.** More self-employed, more non-home-loan. Management's answer is bench quality and improving sequential delinquency, but this is the structural risk to watch over FY28–29 rather than FY27.
6. **30+/90+ ticked up.** *"Minor increase seen in 30+ and 90+ is cyclical in nature and are expected to come down in Q2"* — a dated, checkable claim.
7. **Negative credit cost has a finite life.** The written-off pool is down to ~₹340 crores retail; management guides negative for FY27 only, then normalization — ROA guidance already steps down to 2.3–2.35%.
8. **Fraud-account recovery is entirely optional upside** — nothing budgeted for FY27, timing unknown: *"I can't comment at this point of time because it will depend on the — when I get the buyer."*
9. **Macro:** RBI held repo at 5.25% but cut FY27 GDP *"from 6.9% to 6.66% in its June 2026 policy review"*; the quarter was *"characterized by heightened global uncertainty arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to higher crude oil prices, increased market volatility and tighter liquidity conditions."*
management quality / tone: Confident and unusually specific for a quarter that optically missed. The MD volunteered the recognition change up front rather than letting analysts find it, gave a quantified Q2 bridge (2.5–2.6x Affordable, 60–70% overall net) instead of hiding behind guidance, and refused to soften the Affordable guidance when pressed (*"my guidance will not change, it will continue"*). The CFO handled the NIM walk in full detail (12 bps + 7 bps, plus the Q4 day-count true-up mechanics) without deflecting. Two tells of candour: the admission that Affordable is *"currently less than the target level"*, and the flat refusal to quantify fraud recoveries. The main watch on tone is **repeated reliance on a single unaudited month** — July is cited five separate times as the proof of the turnaround, which is a thin evidentiary base for a 50–60% full-year Affordable growth commitment. Also note the MD twice nudged above his own guidance (*"we should do much better than what we have given guidance"*), which raises the bar he will be judged against.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The 56% vs 18% gap is the whole quarter.** Two headline numbers for the same business, differing only by ~2 months of cheque clearing. Anyone comparing PNBHOUSING's Q1 disbursement growth to peers on a like-for-like basis must use 56%, and the Q2 print will be flattered by the same mechanic in reverse — the sequential number will be structurally overstated.
- **Prime's yield improvement is up-risking, dressed as mix optimization.** *"we have migrated from the composition of more salary to the… rationalized, self-employed segment"* and *"increased our composition from home loan to non-home loan."* ~10–15 bps of the yield came from consuming regulatory (PVC) headroom, not from franchise strength. Absent it, Prime yields would have been *"stable"* at best.
- **The NIM decline is self-inflicted and arguably good.** 12 of the 19 bps came from *deliberately* levering up an over-capitalized balance sheet (3.6 → 3.75 average) — an ROE-accretive trade the P&L presents as margin compression. Only 7 bps was accounting noise, and none of it was competitive pressure.
- **Negative credit cost is flattering a −4pp NII/PAT gap.** NII +6%, PPOP +9%, PAT only +4% — the recovery tailwind (−12 bps) is running *alongside*, not covering, the ₹10–12 crore OTS write-off and the ECL build. Strip both and the underlying earnings quality is thinner than "negative credit cost" suggests.
- **Affordable's quality improved even as its volume disappointed.** BT-in collapsed 10.5% → 3.4%, i.e. the shortfall is in *new-to-market* originations, not in a loss of refinanced book — the harder but more durable kind of growth.
- **The "no new branches" stance is the real opex story.** Three new businesses (Affordable-via-Prime, micro-housing, Emerging Developer Finance) are all being launched into the existing 404-branch footprint, which is why opex/ATA fell below 1% while headcount investment rose.
- **A fraud classification with zero P&L impact is a *recovery* event, not a credit event** — fully provided in FY22-23, and management argues classification *accelerates* resolution: *"generally it expedites because there are legal recourse. Because till the time you take this step, the customer will never come forward to discuss and close it."*

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Strategic Objectives frame "Sustainable Business Growth" around four planks: High Yielding Portfolio Growth, Asset Quality ("Sustain best-in-class asset quality through robust underwriting, rigorous monitoring and continues policy refinements"), Technology & Artificial Intelligence, and Consistent Profitability.
- Deck states "Reinitiate corporate lending with disciplined risk management, capping exposure at under ~10% of the total loan portfolio"; corporate is currently 0.5% of loan asset (30-Jun-26) vs 1.0% (30-Jun-25), and it notes "Corporate NPA Nil since Jun-24".
- Retail franchise scale: "Live loan accounts serviced by the Company crossed 3,87,000 as on 30-Jun-26", with average ticket size of INR 29 lac (Individual Housing) and INR 27 lac (Retail Non-Housing).
- Underwriting posture presented as mid/low-ticket and prime-bureau led: "95% of fresh sanction volume on-boarded has ticket size of less than INR 1 crore" and "87% of the loans booked in Q1 FY27 has financial applicant's bureau score of more than 700".
- Deck benchmarks its Affordable book against industry: "As per ICRA, the 30+ and 90+ delinquencies for AHFCs as on Dec-25 is 3.8% and 1.4%", against Affordable DPD 30+ of 1.60% and Gross NPA of 0.74% in Q1 FY27.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Prime** — ₹3,083 crores disbursed. The yield surprise of the quarter: the segment grew fastest *and* repriced up, entirely on mix. *"there was very tough competition in salaried segment, much in Prime, and that is why we have migrated from the composition of more salary to the… rationalized, self-employed segment. And also we increased our composition from home loan to non-home loan because we were having a good cushion in terms of PVC norms."* Prime yield *"my Q4 was 8.92. So 8 bps growth we have shown till in Q1"*, with *"around 10 to 15 bps benefit we have got by changing the mix."* Absent the mix shift: *"Maybe not gone down, you can say stable."*
- **Emerging Markets** — ₹2,029 crores disbursed; yield *"up 8 basis points"* QoQ (analyst-stated, not disputed). Together with Affordable it is *"our key growth engine, growing 27% Y-o-Y and contributing 41% of retail portfolio."*
- **Affordable** — ₹555 crores net disbursement, the quarter's weak spot. *"We are actively focusing on increasing the productivity of Affordable branches, while select Prime and Emerging Market branches also started contributing to Affordable business"* (≈₹30 crores from those branches in June alone). Yield moved most here: *"my overall yield in Affordable itself has grown by almost 50 bps"* Q4→Q1. Quality of growth improved — Affordable BT-in fell from 10.5% to 3.4%, *"which suggests that the team has started focusing on new customer… it is primarily new customer in the market."*
- **Micro-housing (new this quarter)** — to be run off the existing Affordable branch network, not new infrastructure: *"We will also do currently micro housing business from our Affordable branches. I don't think at this point of time we need to open more number of branches. We will leverage our existing branches to contain our opex also, because that's the key metrics to be watched."*
- **Corporate / construction finance** — ₹493 crores book, being held to *"3% of my overall book in FY27"*; margin-accretive by design.
- No subsidiary or associate was discussed on this call.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
Not an order-book business; the lender-equivalent pipeline this quarter is the **sanctioned-but-unrealized cheque pool** created by the recognition change, plus the new-product ramps.
- **Recognition-change carry-forward:** *"I think it will generally spread across in 2 months forward. So maybe larger portion comes in next month and then some portion comes in second month. Third month is any minuscule business only flow forward… because there's a resale cases there and sometimes seller takes time to execute the transaction."* On the September question: *"It's a cycle now. So cycle is maintained now."*
- **July momentum (post-quarter, pre-call):** *"July already we have witnessed very good momentum in terms of gross and net"*; *"my July month realization is much promising than my — any of the month of last quarter"*; and on Affordable sourced through Prime/Emerging branches, *"it is almost double than what we delivered in Q1, in July itself"* — those branches *"started contributing almost 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July itself."*
- **Emerging Developer Finance (new):** *"we disbursed INR 71 crores under Emerging Developer Finance program."*
- **Loan buyouts (new):** *"we have commenced full buyout transactions and acquired loan assets aggregating to INR146 crores during the quarter."*
- **Corporate book:** ₹493 crores outstanding, ₹215 crores disbursed in Q1 — deliberately capped at 3% of book.
- **PMAY 2.0:** *"we are particularly pleased to have facilitated over 7,000 subsidies under the PMAY 2.0."*

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Loan-book growth FY27: 18%–20%** — *"Maintaining full year guidance of 18% to 20% overall book growth."* Management then went further: *"our team is focusing on better growth than what we have given guidance. I think we should do much better than what we have given guidance."*
- **Affordable loan-book growth FY27: 50%–60%** — *"Also maintaining growth guidance of 50% to 60% in Affordable loan book"*; later restated as *"We said that we will have a growth of around 60% in Affordable, that still we are holding and we will do it. So, my guidance will not change."*
- **Q2 FY27 disbursement step-up (quantified)** — Affordable *"should be 2.5 to 2.6x higher than what we did in Q1"*; overall net *"it should be near 60%-70% higher"* (net-to-net vs Q1). Also *"Expecting Q2 to be much better than Q1, particularly in Affordable business"* and *"we will try to beat both the numbers, which is gross or net."*
- **Mix: Affordable + Emerging = 45% of book by end-FY27, ~50% by FY28** — *"expecting to touch 45% by the end of this year… if I talk about 2-year horizon, it would be nearly 50%"*; restated as *"should contribute 45% of my overall book in FY27, and 50% in FY28."*
- **Construction finance capped** — *"we will restrict it to 3% of my overall book in FY27, which will help us in overall improvement in margin."*
- **Margin: bottomed, improvement from H2 FY27** — *"margin seems to have bottomed out. And from second half onwards, gradually, there should be improvement in margins"*; CFO: *"we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year."* MD adds cost of funds too: *"cost of fund also, we strongly believe that it has also bottomed out."*
- **ROA: ~2.4% FY27, ~2.3–2.35% thereafter** — *"for this year, I think it should be in the range of 2.4%… Next year, this credit cost normalizing, we expect it to be around 2.3%"* and *"on a long-term basis we are expected to settle around 2.3% kind of a ROA, 2.3% to 2.35%."*
- **Credit cost stays negative through FY27** — *"this year I think we should continue to remain negative. We still have line of sight on good recoveries quarter-on-quarter this year at least."*
- **Rating-upgrade CoF benefit ~10 bps** — *"around 10 basis points at least should come in"*, contingent on the pending ICRA/CRISIL actions (see §10).
- **Micro-housing P&L contribution only from H2 FY27** — *"In Q2, the policy was already formulated, is rolled out, people have started sourcing, but real fruit you will be able to see from H2 FY27 onward."*
- **Fee income to track disbursement growth** — *"based on the good disbursement growth, solid performance, the fee income growth should also be in line with the disbursement growth going forward"*; fee income is **not** distorted by the recognition change — *"we still continue to get that amount or fee based on the committed disbursements."*
- **No recovery budgeted from the fraud account in FY27** — *"we have not factored in any recovery this year because this entire legal process may take a time."*

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Emerging Developer Finance** — first ₹71 crores disbursed; explicitly a yield lever: *"as part of our new initiative to augment high-yield portfolio growth."*
- **Full loan buyouts** — ₹146 crores in the first quarter of the programme: *"These initiatives will support faster scale up of the loan book while enhancing portfolio yield and maintaining portfolio quality."*
- **Co-located Affordable sourcing** — Prime/Emerging branches now originating Affordable; *"early results from the co-located branches models have been encouraging"*, ≈15–18% of Affordable business in July.
- **Micro-housing** — policy rolled out, sourcing started; P&L only from H2 FY27.
- **AI / digital stack** — *"Our focus on conversational AI and document intelligence… During the quarter, we successfully completed Voice AI proof-of-concept for the sanctioned but undisbursed pool and pre-due collections with encouraging results, while AI-powered policy and knowledge assistance are currently under evaluation."* Rails already at scale: *"100% of our fresh disbursals are happening through our new LOS platform, which we call SFDC. More than 70% of our business is now being onboarded through our in-house onboarding app, which is the Infinity app. And more than 2,600 e-sign executed through Legality platform."* Plus an *"in-house computing intelligence platform."*
- **Rating-upgrade cycle** — CARE done, *"we are yet to get 2 more upgrades from 2 rating agencies"* (ICRA, CRISIL); *"that is another lever which will help us further on the cost of borrowing side."*

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **NIM 3.50%, −19 bps QoQ**, fully attributed: *"12 bps is attributable to increase in leverage and 7 bps in true-up impact of Q4 FY26."* CFO's fuller version adds the asset-side drag: *"there is also a flow-through impact. If you see, Q4 generally is very high on disbursements, and most of that got realized in the current quarter, and hence it actually translated into higher borrowings during the current quarter. Plus, there is an impact of also on the overall yield being slightly lower while the loan book yield has improved, but overall yield has slightly moderated due to lower investment yields."*
- **Spread held at 2.12%**, book and incremental — *"Despite the prevailing headwinds, we maintained our spread at 2.12%, demonstrating resilience in our business model and disciplined pricing approach."*
- **Yield inflected, barely:** 9.47% → **9.48%**. The bull case rests on mix, not rates: *"there is no further drop expected on the yield perspective, it is only expected to go up. And hence the only positive impact that we see from now on is on account of mix change."*
- **Funding cost is the live headwind:** book CoB 7.35% → **7.36%**, but incremental CoB **+18 bps**. Asked whether it has cooled: *"there is some improvement versus what it was, let's say, at the beginning of the previous quarter, but still it remains elevated."* Offsets claimed: *"now Q2 onwards, with higher contribution of Affordable, CF business and Emerging business, we feel that we will be able to offset the impacts, if any, of cost of borrowing, as well as of any further impact of leverage."*
- **Why last year's mix shift did NOT show in yield** (Renish's challenge — book yield down ~50 bps YoY despite a richer mix): *"last one year, if you see, there is a change in the repo rate also, and the interest rate environment also was different… So our incremental yields have gone down in line with the industry trend. So hence you did not see that kind of a transition impact on the overall book yield."*
- **Opex leverage is real:** opex +10% YoY to ₹237 crores but opex/ATA below 1% (from 1.08% in Q4 FY26); PPOP +9% on NII +6%.
- **Recognition change is yield-neutral, income-negative:** *"The impact is only on interest income for the quarter"*; and *"if you are not booking the underlying loan, you are not booking that income also. So it will not impact your yield. It will impact the absolute income, but it will not impact the yield."*

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Capital position:** CAR 28.26%, Tier 1 27.87%, net worth ₹19,800 crores, book value ~₹760 — *"Our capital position remains strong."* No capital raise, buyback or dividend was discussed on this call.
- **Deployment path** is leverage-up into higher-yield retail: average leverage 3.6 → 3.75, mix to 45% Affordable+Emerging by FY27 and ~50% by FY28, CF capped at 3%.
- **Return framework:** ROE 11.44% on ROA 2.37% — the gap is exactly the under-levered balance sheet; management is guiding ROA down (2.4% → 2.3–2.35%) as credit cost normalizes, implying the ROE story has to come from leverage and mix rather than from asset returns.
- **New capital uses this quarter:** Emerging Developer Finance (₹71 crores) and loan buyouts (₹146 crores) — both explicitly yield-accretive.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and unusually specific for a quarter that optically missed. The MD volunteered the recognition change up front rather than letting analysts find it, gave a quantified Q2 bridge (2.5–2.6x Affordable, 60–70% overall net) instead of hiding behind guidance, and refused to soften the Affordable guidance when pressed (*"my guidance will not change, it will continue"*). The CFO handled the NIM walk in full detail (12 bps + 7 bps, plus the Q4 day-count true-up mechanics) without deflecting. Two tells of candour: the admission that Affordable is *"currently less than the target level"*, and the flat refusal to quantify fraud recoveries. The main watch on tone is **repeated reliance on a single unaudited month** — July is cited five separate times as the proof of the turnaround, which is a thin evidentiary base for a 50–60% full-year Affordable growth commitment. Also note the MD twice nudged above his own guidance (*"we should do much better than what we have given guidance"*), which raises the bar he will be judged against.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)
moat.body:
- **Capital as an optionality buffer** — CAR 28.26% / Tier 1 27.87% against period-end leverage of 3.72x. Management is deliberately *spending* this cushion (average leverage 3.6 → 3.75) to fund growth, i.e. NIM dilution here is a chosen use of surplus capital, not distress.
- **Underwriting bench in self-employed mortgages** — the defence offered for pushing Prime up-risk into self-employed and non-home-loan: *"while my yield has gone up, I would say sequentially even my delinquency in Prime and Emerging has improved from last quarter because team is a very seasoned underwriting team… we have good seasoned expertise team in underwriting, especially in the self-employed segment."* Evidenced by the direction of 30+/90+ within Prime/Emerging, though the aggregate 30+/90+ did tick up.
- **Regulatory headroom as a pricing lever** — the Prime mix shift into non-home-loan was executed *"because we were having a good cushion in terms of PVC norms. So regulatory also we were very much in line."* — i.e. unused regulatory capacity converted directly into ~10–15 bps of yield.
- **Distribution + own-tech rails** — 404 branches with the ability to originate a *different* segment (Affordable) off existing Prime/Emerging infrastructure at no incremental opex; 100% of fresh disbursals on the in-house LOS.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **The Q2 catch-up must actually land.** The whole quarter's optics are deferred, not lost — but only if realization follows: overall net disbursement *"near 60%-70% higher"* than Q1 and Affordable *"2.5 to 2.6x"*. Miss this and FY27's 18–20% book guidance is at risk.
2. **Incremental cost of borrowing +18 bps and still elevated.** Management concedes it *"still remains elevated"*; the NIM-bottoming call depends on mix-driven yield gains offsetting it.
3. **Pending rating upgrades are unpriced and undated.** *"CARE is already done. ICRA is underway. I think we are expecting very soon. ICRA and CRISIL is underway."* Worth *"around 10 basis points at least"* on CoF — but no date was given (deliberately excluded from `near_term_trigger`, see §10 rule).
4. **Affordable is behind plan, and the fix is a brand-new leadership team.** ₹555 crores is *"currently less than the target level"*; the recovery case is entirely *"under new leadership team, particularly new CBO"* with one month (July) of evidence.
5. **Prime is being pushed up-risk.** More self-employed, more non-home-loan. Management's answer is bench quality and improving sequential delinquency, but this is the structural risk to watch over FY28–29 rather than FY27.
6. **30+/90+ ticked up.** *"Minor increase seen in 30+ and 90+ is cyclical in nature and are expected to come down in Q2"* — a dated, checkable claim.
7. **Negative credit cost has a finite life.** The written-off pool is down to ~₹340 crores retail; management guides negative for FY27 only, then normalization — ROA guidance already steps down to 2.3–2.35%.
8. **Fraud-account recovery is entirely optional upside** — nothing budgeted for FY27, timing unknown: *"I can't comment at this point of time because it will depend on the — when I get the buyer."*
9. **Macro:** RBI held repo at 5.25% but cut FY27 GDP *"from 6.9% to 6.66% in its June 2026 policy review"*; the quarter was *"characterized by heightened global uncertainty arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to higher crude oil prices, increased market volatility and tighter liquidity conditions."*

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The 56% vs 18% gap is the whole quarter.** Two headline numbers for the same business, differing only by ~2 months of cheque clearing. Anyone comparing PNBHOUSING's Q1 disbursement growth to peers on a like-for-like basis must use 56%, and the Q2 print will be flattered by the same mechanic in reverse — the sequential number will be structurally overstated.
- **Prime's yield improvement is up-risking, dressed as mix optimization.** *"we have migrated from the composition of more salary to the… rationalized, self-employed segment"* and *"increased our composition from home loan to non-home loan."* ~10–15 bps of the yield came from consuming regulatory (PVC) headroom, not from franchise strength. Absent it, Prime yields would have been *"stable"* at best.
- **The NIM decline is self-inflicted and arguably good.** 12 of the 19 bps came from *deliberately* levering up an over-capitalized balance sheet (3.6 → 3.75 average) — an ROE-accretive trade the P&L presents as margin compression. Only 7 bps was accounting noise, and none of it was competitive pressure.
- **Negative credit cost is flattering a −4pp NII/PAT gap.** NII +6%, PPOP +9%, PAT only +4% — the recovery tailwind (−12 bps) is running *alongside*, not covering, the ₹10–12 crore OTS write-off and the ECL build. Strip both and the underlying earnings quality is thinner than "negative credit cost" suggests.
- **Affordable's quality improved even as its volume disappointed.** BT-in collapsed 10.5% → 3.4%, i.e. the shortfall is in *new-to-market* originations, not in a loss of refinanced book — the harder but more durable kind of growth.
- **The "no new branches" stance is the real opex story.** Three new businesses (Affordable-via-Prime, micro-housing, Emerging Developer Finance) are all being launched into the existing 404-branch footprint, which is why opex/ATA fell below 1% while headcount investment rose.
- **A fraud classification with zero P&L impact is a *recovery* event, not a credit event** — fully provided in FY22-23, and management argues classification *accelerates* resolution: *"generally it expedites because there are legal recourse. Because till the time you take this step, the customer will never come forward to discuss and close it."*

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First note for PNBHOUSING in this corpus. Disbursement recognition switched to cheque-realization (56% → 18% reported YoY growth); loan book ₹89,670 cr (+15%); PAT ₹557 cr (+4%); NIM 3.50% (−19 bps QoQ) with spread flat at 2.12%; GNPA 0.95%; credit cost negative 12 bps on ₹67 cr written-off-pool recovery; CAR 28.26%. Affordable disbursement ₹555 cr, below target; new CBO in place. Guidance unchanged: **18–20% book growth, 50–60% Affordable growth, ROA ~2.4%, NIM improving from H2 FY27**. Quantified Q2 step-up: overall net disbursement *"near 60%-70% higher"*, Affordable *"2.5 to 2.6x"*.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did net disbursements land ~60–70% above Q1's ₹5,882 cr and Affordable ~2.5–2.6x ₹555 cr; (b) did 30+/90+ come down as promised; (c) did ICRA/CRISIL upgrades land and did CoB fall ~10 bps; (d) is spread still ≥2.12% and did NIM stop falling; (e) Affordable+Emerging share progress from 41% toward 45%; (f) is credit cost still negative and what is left of the ~₹340 cr written-off pool._
